Condition: Include this section if ANY of the recommendations involve replacing one financial product with another.

Create one sub-section for each product being replaced. Do not combine multiple products into a single switching disclosure.

Adapt the heading to the product type: "Consequences of Replacing Your Pension", "Consequences of Replacing Your Investment Platform", etc.

This section must appear in full in this document and cannot be incorporated by reference.

Replacing Your [PRODUCT NAME] - [EXISTING PROVIDER] to [NEW PROVIDER]

Repeat this sub-section for each product being replaced.

Costs on Disposal

State the costs the client will incur by exiting their existing product. Address each of the following:

(a) Exit fees: State the pound amount, or "No exit fee applies." Most modern funds and platforms do not charge exit fees, but older products may.

(b) Buy/sell spreads on disposal: If units must be redeemed, calculate the sell spread cost. E.g., "Sell spread of 0.10% on £385,773 = approximately £386."

(c) Capital gains tax (CGT): "Selling existing investments may crystallise a capital gains tax liability. Based on the unrealised gains in your portfolio of £[AMOUNT], the estimated tax impact is £[AMOUNT], depending on your annual exempt amount and applicable CGT rate. This is a tax matter - please confirm the exact impact with your tax adviser before proceeding."

If unrealised gains data is not available: "Selling existing investments may crystallise capital gains. The tax impact depends on your unrealised gains, your remaining annual exempt amount and your applicable CGT rate. Please consult your tax adviser. [TBC - tax estimate to be confirmed.]"

(d) Pension transfers only: if the existing scheme has a defined benefit (safeguarded benefits) component and the transfer value exceeds the level at which regulated pension transfer advice is mandatory, state this and confirm that separate qualifying pension transfer advice from a Pension Transfer Specialist has been, or will be, obtained. This document does not itself constitute that advice.

[COSTS ON DISPOSAL - pound amounts]

Costs on Acquisition

State the costs the client will incur on establishing the new product. Address:

(a) Application/establishment fees: Pound amount or "Nil."

(b) Buy/sell spreads on acquisition: If units must be purchased, calculate the buy spread cost.

(c) In-specie transfer limitations: "The following holdings [can / cannot] be transferred in-specie (without selling and repurchasing): [LIST]. Holdings that cannot be transferred will need to be sold on the existing platform and repurchased on the new platform, incurring buy/sell spreads and potential tax consequences."

(d) Cash requirements: "The new [platform/scheme] requires a minimum cash holding of £[AMOUNT]. This may require selling £[AMOUNT] of existing investments to meet the cash requirement."

(e) Expression of Wish: "You will need to complete a new Expression of Wish nomination for the new scheme - your existing nomination does not transfer automatically."

[COSTS ON ACQUISITION - pound amounts and conditions]

sections.title: Benefits You Will Lose
sections.guidance:
This section is mandatory when a product is being replaced. Complete it thoroughly.

Address each of the following explicitly. If a point does not apply, state that rather than omitting it:

(a) Grandfathered fee arrangements:

"Your existing [PRODUCT] was established on [DATE / before DATE]. [If grandfathered fees apply: Your current fee of [X]% is a grandfathered rate that is no longer available to new members. Moving to a new product means you will pay the current published rate of [X]%.] [If no grandfathered fees: We are not aware of any grandfathered fee arrangements on your existing product.]"

(b) Expression of Wish:

"Your current Expression of Wish nomination on [FUND NAME] will not transfer automatically. If you transfer your balance from this scheme, you must complete a new Expression of Wish nomination on the new scheme, or your death benefits may be paid at the new scheme administrator's discretion without your wishes on record."

(c) Employer contribution arrangements:

If the current scheme receives employer pension contributions: "Your employer currently contributes to [FUND NAME]. You will need to update your pension scheme nomination with your employer to redirect contributions to the new scheme. During the transition, there may be a short period where contributions are directed to the old scheme."

(d) Defined benefit entitlements:

If the current scheme has a defined benefit (safeguarded benefits) component: "Your [FUND NAME] includes a defined benefit component. Transferring out of a defined benefit scheme is generally an irreversible decision. The defined benefit formula entitles you to [DETAIL]. Where the cash equivalent transfer value exceeds the level at which regulated advice is mandatory, this transfer cannot proceed without qualifying pension transfer advice from a Pension Transfer Specialist, obtained separately from this document. Before proceeding, you should obtain a current transfer value from the scheme trustee." [This is a HIGH-RISK switching scenario - flag prominently.]

If not a defined benefit scheme, state: "Your existing scheme is a defined contribution arrangement and does not include a defined benefit component."

(e) Unique investment options:

If the current product offers investment options not available on the new product (e.g., specific unlisted property funds, direct property, specific manager strategies), flag these.

(f) Loyalty or continuity benefits:

Fee discounts for tenure, bonus units, guaranteed annuity rates, or other loyalty features that would be lost.

[BENEFITS LOST - specific and itemised]

sections.title: Other Significant Consequences
sections.guidance:
Address any other material consequences not covered above. At minimum:

Market exposure during transition: "There may be a period of [X] business days during the transfer where your funds are in transit and not invested. During this period, you will not benefit from market gains but will also not be exposed to market falls. This period is typically 3-10 business days for pension transfers."

Tax-free cash already taken: "Once tax-free cash (Pension Commencement Lump Sum) has been taken from a pension, it cannot be re-taken from a new arrangement on transfer. Your current tax-free cash taken to date is £[AMOUNT] ([X]% of the crystallised fund)." If this is not known: "[TBC - tax-free cash taken to date to be confirmed from the existing scheme.]"

Means-tested state benefits implications (if applicable): If the client receives any means-tested state benefits, note any implications of changing products on the assessment of those benefits.

Lost contribution history / continuity: Some schemes use contribution or membership history for loyalty pricing or guaranteed rates. This may be lost on transfer.

Capital at Risk:

The value of investments and the income from them can go down as well as up. You may get back less than the amount you originally invested. Past performance is not a reliable indicator of future results.

Inflation Risk:

The purchasing power of your investments may be eroded over time if investment returns do not keep pace with inflation. This is particularly relevant to cash holdings and lower-risk investments.

Pension Access:

Tax & Legislation:
